title: Prefix extraction from a pair encoding
statement: For any bit strings $a$ and $b$, the prefix extractor, started on the encoding that doubles each bit of $a$, appends the separator $01$, and then appends $b$, halts within $|\langle a,b\rangle|+1$ steps and outputs the first $|a|$ bits of $b$, or all of $b$ if $|b|<|a|$.
replaced: For all bit strings $a$ and $b$, the prefix-extraction machine $E$ (one work tape, four states; it counts the data blocks of a pair encoding in unary and then copies that many payload bits), started on the self-delimiting pair encoding $\langle a,b\rangle$, halts within $|\langle a,b\rangle| + 1$ steps with output exactly the first $|a|$ bits of $b$ (all of $b$ if $|b| < |a|$).
